title: Quiz Game
story: 'What's the capital of France?' If you answered 'Paris', you scored a point. Now imagine a quiz with 10 questions, scoring, and a results summary. Build the quiz engine — the same structure that powers trivia nights, exam prep, and BuzzFeed quizzes.
why: A quiz game teaches structs for questions, Vec for question banks, scoring logic with conditionals, and results display — a complete interactive program.
analogy: A game show buzzer: the host reads a question, you buzz in with an answer, the scoreboard lights up or doesn't. Your quiz engine is the entire show — question bank (script), answer checking (judge), scoring (scoreboard), and final results (the big reveal).
try_it: Add multiple choice: each question has 4 options, only one correct. Add categories (Science, History, Sports) and let players choose a category. Track time per question. Add a high score system that persists across multiple quiz runs.
tips: Store questions in a Vec — easy to add, remove, or shuffle
Compare answers case-insensitively for better user experience
common_mistakes: Hardcoding answer checking instead of using the stored correct_answer
Comparing strings with == without handling case differences
Not handling the case where total questions is zero (division by zero)
